comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C9-C10, C50-C56, C91 regarding N162 glycan's role in mediating kifunensine effects on ADCC. Both evaluations find the evidence compelling and well-supported by experimental data across fucosylated and afucosylated antibodies.

Perfect agreement on claims C97-C100 regarding the entropy-based mechanistic model. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to simplifying assumptions and lack of direct thermodynamic measurements, while peer reviewers accept the mechanistic interpretation without challenge, describing it as demonstrating a mechanistic link.

Both address claim C92 about N162 glycan heterogeneity providing a range of ADCC potency. OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED based on established links, while peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, noting that natural regulation and variability require future investigation.

Strong agreement on claims C6-C7, C43-C49 regarding glycosidase treatment experiments and N162 glycan's predominant role. Both evaluations find the systematic approach and quantitative data highly convincing and well-supported.

Agreement on claims C11, C72, C74-C77 regarding NMR spectroscopy data showing chemical shift perturbations and correlation with affinity. Both evaluations affirm the NMR-based mechanistic model as compelling and significant.

Strong agreement on claims C38-C42 regarding N162 glycan's role in baseline affinity and fucose sensitivity. Both evaluations support the findings, with peer reviewers noting this fills a critical knowledge gap about glycosylation-sensitive IgG-FcR interaction.

Agreement on claims C62-C67 regarding NMR spectroscopy technical achievement and assignment percentages. Both evaluations strongly affirm the NMR work as highly compelling and methodologically rigorous, recognizing it as a major contribution.

Agreement on claims C101-C108 regarding W90/W113 functional importance and conservation patterns. Both evaluations accept the residue-level analysis and functional validation through ADCC assays without critique.

Agreement on claims C23-C30 regarding mutagenesis screen and affinity measurements. Both evaluations support the systematic identification of hotspot regions, with peer reviewers praising the well-designed mutation strategy and exhaustive biophysical measurements.

Agreement on claims C93-C95 regarding the ~300 nM affinity threshold for ADCC. Both evaluations accept the affinity-function relationship and therapeutic implications, though OpenEval notes the exact threshold may be approximate and extrapolation beyond tested range.

Agreement on claims C31-C35 regarding affinity-ADCC correlation. Both evaluations support the findings linking higher affinity variants with greater ADCC, with peer reviewers describing the overall work as very strong.

Agreement on claims C86-C90 regarding R155/(1)GlcNAc interactions from MD simulations. Both evaluations accept the structural/MD findings and validation through mutagenesis, with peer reviewers finding the integrated structural data highly compelling.

Agreement on claims C12, C80, C83-C85, C96 regarding conformational dynamics and mechanistic model from converging NMR, crystallography, and MD evidence. Both evaluations support the integration of multiple lines of evidence.

Agreement on claims C112-C113 regarding therapeutic implications of small affinity improvements. Both evaluations accept these forward-looking conclusions, with peer reviewers affirming the work will be of significant interest to therapeutic antibody design.
Agreement on claim C111 regarding engineering strategy for variants with higher affinity than V158. Both evaluations support this as a valid conclusion from the data with therapeutic implications.

Agreement on claims C60-C61, C68, C71 regarding comparative NMR analysis and minimal backbone perturbation at glycosylation sites. Both evaluations affirm the methodological rigor and surprising findings.
Agreement on claims C69-C70 regarding established structural knowledge. Both evaluations accept these as providing necessary context for interpreting experimental results.

Agreement on claims C78-C79, C81-C82 regarding structural analysis from X-ray crystallography. Both evaluations support the structural comparisons identifying conformational differences relevant to binding mechanism.

Agreement on claims C109-C110 regarding K161's surprising effect on affinity without direct Fc contact. Both evaluations accept the finding, though OpenEval notes the stabilization inference is speculative.
Agreement on claim C107 regarding established sequence knowledge. Both evaluations accept this as providing necessary context for experimental results.
